the self-criticism of perfectionists may be triggered by the stress of work, and that this stress may be compounded by their perseverative cognitive styles.

self-critical perfectionists are more vulnerable than non-perfectionists to the detrimental effects of perseverative cognition, and thus, to the negative consequences of respite from work (and other achievement-related stressors).

The main takeaway from our work is that

the self-criticism of perfectionists is a key factor in their tendency to perseverate about work during respite and that this tendency to perseverate can lead to a deterioration in well-being when they return to work.
the self-criticism of perfectionists is not only a problem in itself, but it also makes them vulnerable to perseverative thinking and to the negative effects of this type of thinking.

self-critical perfectionists may benefit from being encouraged to take respite from their work and from being provided with strategies to manage their perseverative cognitions when they return to work.
